AP Art: 2D Art and Design


Oct 2022 - May 2023

Sustained Investigation: How does trauma affect my perception of myself and my surroundings? The struggle of moving forward leaves me trapped in an inescapable nightmare, which I’d like to examine through distortion of self-image/ worldview using filters. I wish to probe the depths of my paranoia through chaotic composition, movement, and progression. Using myself as a subject, I want to explore the effect of color or lack thereof to authentically represent the visceral emotions I portray in their turbulent environments. How do my emotions change my reality? How do they create multiple layers that warp the truth?

Written Evidence: Self-portraits were the most authentic subject of my works, and as I progressed, so did the complexity per iteration. I started to examine perception disembodiment with the eyes (2) but realized the pervasiveness that extended to all 5 senses (3). I explored the passage of time through composition (4,7,8), using colored film(6,9), and 3-D media to separate the planes/surfaces of my work (3,9,14). Color and grayscale distinguish between my reality and truth (4,5,10,15). Seeking to further the chaos, I collaged small boxes that represented my paranoia, juxtaposing my figure multiple times (14).

title: AP Art: Drawing
description: My AP Art exam from senior year of high school
overlayHTML:
AP Art: Drawing


Oct 2023 - May 2024

Sustained Investigation: Varnam, the crowning centerpiece of a Bharathanatyam repertoire. A representation of all dance can be, alternating lyrical stanzas and rhythmic sequences. While learning and practicing I notice my portrayal of seemingly opposing concepts simultaneously: stillness/movement, physical/emotional, imagination/reality that culminate in performance. How has learning the varnam helped me make these connections within this dynamic interplay of paradoxical concepts? How do they influence each other? Focusing on juxtaposition, I wish to explore the capacity of motionless art to convey this complexity.

Written Evidence: Focusing on juxtaposition, I experimented with composition, painting linear frames like animation, collaging(7,8), creating tunnel books(5), and using laser engraving(6) to portray more abstract concepts like practice, performance, stillness, and imagination.I practiced anatomy & facial expressions to bring out nuances in emotion and accentuate differences between figures (3,5). I worked on detail, leading me to revise my depiction of linear motion (2,4,9). I discovered that the 4 pillars I’d established interplay and intersect with each other, which I synthesized in works (13, 14, 15)

Here are some of the pieces!
